clue.text: In workplace boy restrains urge

indicators.note: restrains means the boy's name holds the urge inside it, like a captor

parts.note: Ken is a boy's name
an itch is an urge or craving

explanation.surface: At work, a lad keeps a powerful craving in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link word joining the definition to the wordplay, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen is a room where cooks and chefs do their job, so it is a place of work.

clue.text: Australian bouncer tops attempt to win — non-striker's case here considered

indicators.note: tops means the first piece sits above the second in this down answer

parts.note: a kangaroo is the bounding Australian animal
to court is to try to win someone's affection

explanation.surface: A big Aussie doorman tries his luck while a cricket non-striker's case is discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' and 'non-striker' suggest a nightclub doorman and cricket; the definition means strikebreakers tried by an unofficial union tribunal.
explanation.definitionFit: An unofficial, irregular tribunal, such as strikers might hold to judge a colleague who refused to strike.

clue.text: During Questions MP, first among equals, provokes violent uproar

indicators.note: during means the following pieces happen inside the questions

parts.note: a test is a set of questions
taken as written

indicators.note: first among means take the opening letter of equals

explanation.surface: At Question Time a member of parliament, first among equals, causes an uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provokes' is a link word. 'First among equals' looks like the stock phrase for a prime minister but just supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, and figuratively a violent commotion or uproar.

clue.text: Hard currency advanced to scavenger

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
the yen is the currency of Japan
A stands for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Hard cash is lent to someone who lives off scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is an African carnivore known for feeding on carcasses killed by others.

clue.text: Earn half-heartedly after stick up liberates zero cash

indicators.note: after means the earnings piece follows the stick
up turns the stick backwards, as it reads bottom to top in a down answer

parts.note: a baton is a stick, such as a police truncheon

indicators.note: half-heartedly means one of the two middle letters of earn is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter

explanation.surface: A mugger's stick-up robs a poor worker of every penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BATON into NOTAB; 'half-heartedly' drops R, one of the two middle letters, leaving EAN. 'liberates' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having no money whatsoever, completely broke.

clue.text: People accepting help first

indicators.note: accepting means the people take the help in, so it sits inside them

parts.note: men is a common crossword synonym for people
aid means help

explanation.surface: A crowd of people takes assistance before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden voyage or speech is the very first one, so the adjective means first.

clue.text: Small-time?

parts.note: read one way it means tiny; read another it is a short unit of time on the clock

explanation.definitionFit: The word means tiny when stressed on the second syllable and sixty seconds when stressed on the first.

clue.text: In cover for one much-enraged snake-slayer

indicators.note: cover for means the first word wraps around the rearranged letters

parts.note: taken as written, split around the rest

indicators.note: enraged means wildly angry, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Inside a shelter, someone is furious at a snake killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover for' splits the first word so it wraps around the rearrangement of 'one much', which 'enraged' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The ichneumon, or Egyptian mongoose, was famed in antiquity as a killer of snakes and crocodiles.

clue.text: Thus doc achieves promotion within hospital department furthest off

indicators.note: within means the reversed pieces sit inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

indicators.note: achieves promotion means moving upward, so the pieces read bottom to top in a down answer

parts.note: so means thus
MD, Doctor of Medicine, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor finally gets promoted within the furthest-flung hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'achieves promotion' turns both short pieces together, giving DMOS; in a down answer moving up means reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means situated at the very end, the most remote or furthest away.

clue.text: Last but one in political residence

definitions.meaning: in a cricket batting order of eleven, the batter at this position goes in second to last
the British prime minister lives at 10 Downing Street, known by its house number

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between the two definitions. In cricket the batting order runs from one to eleven, so the tenth batter is last but one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten is the second-to-last slot of eleven in cricket, and 10 Downing Street is the prime minister's home.

clue.text: Water-monster from filthy drain

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the next words

explanation.surface: A monster lurking in the water comes out of a dirty drain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra was the many-headed serpent of Greek myth that lived in the marshes of Lerna.

clue.text: In choppy sea Argo is fast up to a point

indicators.note: choppy describes rough water, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: In rough waters, the ship Argo still makes good speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word. The Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to a limited extent, only partially, which is what the phrase about a point conveys.

clue.text: One near Barking stadium

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of the next word go crazily out of order

explanation.surface: Someone living close to a sports ground in the London district of Barking.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, which makes it look like a place name; here it means 'mad' and rearranges NEAR to RENA.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space for sport or spectacle, much the same thing as a stadium.

clue.text: Gambler leaving in happier financial circumstances

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler
off means leaving, as in 'I'm off'

explanation.surface: A punter walks away from the bookmaker richer than before.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone whose money situation has improved, wealthier than before.

clue.text: First couple of pieces in coat tailored where sharper look sold

indicators.note: tailored means cut and reshaped, so the collected letters are rearranged
first couple of means take the opening two letters of the word pieces

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple of pieces of cloth are set into a coat at the tailor's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored' rearranges PI, IN and COAT together; 'First couple of' takes PI from 'pieces'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles sold by an eye specialist let customers see more sharply, so the shop is where a sharper look is sold.

clue.text: Uniform-free messenger loading with spice

indicators.note: loading means the remaining letters take the extra piece on board, inside them
free means without, so the uniform letter is removed

parts.note: a courier carries messages and parcels
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet
and means with, joining things together

explanation.surface: A delivery rider out of uniform loads up with seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' drops the uniform letter from the messenger, leaving CORIER; 'loading' then takes the joining word on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriander is a herb whose dried seeds are used as a spice in cooking.

clue.text: Brawling sir met biblical hit-man

indicators.note: brawling means fighting wildly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A fighting knight encounters an Old Testament assassin.
explanation.definitionFit: Smite is the Bible's word for strike, so one who smites is a scriptural striker.

clue.text: Scary snooker player's relation to pocket

indicators.note: to pocket means the snooker player holds the relation inside, like a ball in a pocket

parts.note: Ding Junhui is a Chinese professional snooker player
an aunt is a relation

explanation.surface: A snooker player's relative is a frightening opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: Ding Junhui is a leading Chinese snooker player; 'pocket' fits snooker but here means contain.
explanation.definitionFit: Daunting means intimidating, likely to discourage or frighten, much like scary.

clue.text: Girl finds secluded place in church

indicators.note: in places the hideaway inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a lair is a hidden retreat or den

explanation.surface: A young woman discovers a quiet hideaway inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Claire is a girl's name, a female forename.

clue.text: Roaming freely — in a big way!

definitions.meaning: escaped and on the loose, as a prisoner who has got away
read literally, the phrase means on a big scale

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means free and uncaptured, and read literally it means in a big or large way.

clue.text: Arrest with admission to prison is for illegal drug supply

indicators.note: with admission to means the arrest piece comes in after the prison piece, entering it

parts.note: can is slang for prison
nab means to catch or arrest
taken as written

explanation.surface: An arrest followed by a spell inside is the penalty for dealing drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is a narcotic plant, illegal in many places, and the word also names a quantity of the drug.

clue.text: Lamb's comments about bread fruit

indicators.note: about means the lamb's sounds go round the bread

parts.note: baas are the bleats a lamb makes
naan, also spelt nan, is an Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: A lamb bleats about bread and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas are a tropical fruit growing in bunches.

clue.text: Indians taking time aboard old steamer

indicators.note: aboard means the time goes on board the steamer, inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Native Americans spend a long time on an old steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people of the Great Plains, formerly called Indians.

clue.text: Hideous Yankee cracking universal mirror at home

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: cracking means the letter breaks into the mirror, sitting inside it

parts.note: a glass is a looking-glass, a mirror
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
in means at home

explanation.surface: An ugly American smashes a mirror while staying in.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile means extremely unattractive, so it matches hideous closely.

clue.text: Painter shows UK ships in Orient after ousting Asians' leader

indicators.note: in places the ships inside what remains of the Orient
after ousting means the Orient word loses a letter before the ships go in

parts.note: the Orient is the East

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Asians'

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is the UK's fleet of ships

explanation.surface: An artist depicts British naval vessels in the Far East once an Asian chief is deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' is a link word; dropping the Asian leader from the Orient leaves EST, around which the fleet goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born surrealist and Dada painter.

clue.text: Some sausages sent to German city

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few sausages are shipped off to a city in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'to', a link word joining the wordplay to the definition; the definition is just 'German city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Couple minus energy "bloody knackered"

indicators.note: minus means the energy letter is taken away

parts.note: to tie is to couple or join
E is the physics symbol for energy
red is the colour of blood

explanation.surface: A pair, now drained of all energy, are utterly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knackered' is British slang for exhausted; 'bloody' here is a colour, not the British intensifier it seems to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Knackered is British slang for worn out, the same meaning as very weary.

clue.text: Lass doing arrangement with note series rapidly executed

indicators.note: an arrangement is a musical rearrangement, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A girl is busy making a musical arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a rapid slide through successive pitches is a glide played up or down a scale.

clue.text: Society girls receptive to scripture study in ruins

indicators.note: receptive to means the society girls take the study in, surrounding it

parts.note: debs are debutantes, young women entering high society
RI is religious instruction, school scripture lessons

explanation.surface: Debutantes take up Bible lessons amid the ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered rubble and wreckage left when something is destroyed.

clue.text: Start rock band

definitions.meaning: a start or origin, the beginning of something
the English progressive rock group fronted by Peter Gabriel and later Phil Collins

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an origin or beginning, and it is also the name of a famous British rock group.
